chunks: My father narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Harun b. al-Jahm from al-Mufaddal b. Salih from Sa'd b. Turayf from Abi Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:

There are three types of injustice: an injustice that Allah will forgive, an injustice that He will not forgive, and an injustice that He will not neglect. As for the injustice that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will not forgive, it is associating partners with Allah (shirk). As for the injustice that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will forgive, it is when a man wrongs himself in what is between him and Allah the Mighty and Majestic. As for the injustice that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will not neglect, it is the ill-treatment among the servants.

key_terms.الشِّرْك: associating partners with Allah (shirk) — the gravest sin in Islam
key_terms.الظُّلْم: injustice / wrongdoing (zulm) — a comprehensive term covering any form of transgression
key_terms.الْمُدَايَنَة: ill-treatment / mutual grievances between people — refers to interpersonal injustice

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of injustice according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) presents a tripartite classification of injustice (zulm) rooted in Quranic theology: (1) shirk — associating partners with Allah — which is the only sin Allah will never forgive (cf. Quran 4:48), (2) sins against oneself in one's relationship with Allah, which Allah may forgive through repentance and mercy, and (3) injustice against other people, which Allah will not let go unpunished because the rights of the wronged must be restored. This framework was foundational in Shia ethical-legal thought for distinguishing between the rights of Allah (huquq Allah) and the rights of people (huquq al-nas).
